equivalence: 프로젝트 조사→Launch/Doctor/Drive/Evidence/Cleanup/Helpers 생성→3~5개 기능 지도→실제 기능 1개의 종단 실행 및 증거 보존→유지보수 안내 5단계를 보존. 플랫폼 종속 생성 경로 3구간만 치환하고 예시 참고 파일 3개는 바이트 그대로 보존. 실제 실행하지 않은 생성 스킬을 산출물로 인정하지 않는 기준도 동일.
checks: exact reviewed replacements; all other bytes preserved

rewrites.before: Every serious project needs a scripted way to drive the real app and prove behavior: launch it, exercise a feature the way a user would, and capture evidence. This skill generates that as a project-local skill (`.cursor/skills/verify-<app>/`) tailored to the repo. You write the generator's output for the next agent, not for a human: it will be read cold, mid-task, by an agent that has never seen the app.

rewrites.before: Create `.cursor/skills/verify-<app>/features/README.md` plus one file per user-facing feature you can identify (aim for the top 3-5 to start, from routes, commands, menus, or docs). Follow the shape in [`references/feature-map-example/`](references/feature-map-example/), with a README index and one file per feature. Each file answers, from the user's point of view: what the feature is, how to reach it, how to drive it with the harness, and what observable end state proves it works. The four H2s are `Sub-features`, `How to get to it (user POV)`, `Driving it with <harness>`, and `Gotchas`. If the seed data lacks a precondition that a journey needs, the journey reports a failure and the reason goes in that feature's `Gotchas`. Never weaken the journey to make it pass. The map is the repo's maintained verification source; a proof that drives one convenient entry point is incomplete when the map lists others.
